ARES.thesis_one_line: Alternative-investment manager (mostly private credit and real assets) earning recurring fees on $671 billion of client money, growing management fees about 15% a year.
kill_criteria: Fee-paying AUM growth below 10% YoY in two consecutive quarterly releases (Q2-26: $409.9bn, +17%).
FRE margin below 40.0% in any quarter (Q2-26: 42.2%).
After-tax realized income per share below the year-earlier quarter in two consecutive quarters (Q2-26: $1.29 vs $1.03).
Quarterly common dividend cut below $1.35 per share (declared for 30 Sep 2026).
Corporate net debt (Debt obligations less corporate cash, consolidated balance sheet, excluding consolidated funds) above 3.0x trailing four-quarter FRE (30 Jun 2026: about 2.1x).
key_adverse_facts: Management fee growth slowed to +15% in Q2-26 from +25% in Q1-26; effective fee rate 0.97% vs 1.00%
Dividend $1.35/quarter equals 100% of trailing four-quarter after-tax realized income per share ($5.17) and 106.7% of H1-26
Section 36(b) derivative suit filed 26 May 2026 in S.D.N.Y. alleging excessive advisory fees paid by ARCC
Q3-26 realized net performance income preliminarily about $10m vs $9m, no carry tailwind (8-K 2026-09-30)
Consensus FY26 $5.84 requires H2 $3.31 vs H1 $2.53 (+31%)
data_conflicts: Yahoo total debt $14.9bn and triage 9.1x leverage include non-recourse consolidated-fund debt (CLO $6,951.7m, fund borrowings $2,531.2m); corporate debt is $4,577.2m, about 2.1x trailing FRE
Yahoo trailing P/E 55.7x uses GAAP EPS $2.19; after-tax realized income trailing is $5.17 (23.6x)
ARES.confidence_in_thesis: medium: fee base is recurring and well disclosed, but the valuation margin of safety is thin and depends on fundraising and private-credit sentiment

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for ARES. Own reverse DCF implies 8.1% a year of 10-year growth versus my 10% base (implied below base, thin margin: 8.8% at NTM $5.40).

ARES.scenario_basis: NTM after-tax realized income $5.70/share; growth 4%/12%/17% a year; exit 13x/18x/22x NTM; dividend $5.40 flat/+8%/+12%; start price $122.01

CLX.thesis_one_line: Maker of Clorox, Glad, Brita, Hidden Valley and Purell with slipping underlying sales and heavy new debt; cheap, but proof of recovery is still missing.
kill_criteria: FY27 adjusted EPS guidance low end cut below $5.70 at any quarterly release (current "between $5.70 and $6.00").
Organic sales growth below 0% in each of Q2 FY27 and Q3 FY27 (quarters free of the ERP lap).
Consolidated net debt (notes and loans payable + current maturities + long-term debt - cash) above 4.0x GAAP EBITDA at 30 Jun 2027 (30 Jun 2026: 4.2x).
Full-year FY27 gross margin below 41.0% (guide about 42%; FY26 42.3%).
FY27 reported free cash flow (operating cash flow less capex) below total dividends paid ($602m in FY26), or any dividend cut.
key_adverse_facts: FY26 adjusted EPS guidance cut on 30 Apr 2026 from $5.95-$6.30 to $5.45-$5.65; actual $5.53
Net debt $4,925m (consolidated, 30 Jun 2026), about 4.2x GAAP EBITDA after GOJO ($2.15bn, debt-funded) and $476m Glad stake purchase
Reported FY26 free cash flow $405m vs dividends $602m; company adjusted FCF $881m adds back the $476m payment
FY27 organic sales guide +3.5% to +4.5% includes more than 3.5 points from lapping ERP drawdown, so underlying about 0% to +1%
S&P long-term rating BBB at 30 Jun 2026 vs BBB+ a year earlier
data_conflicts: Yahoo free cash flow $110m vs filing OCF $612m less capex $207m = $405m
Yahoo total debt $5,598m includes about $452m operating leases; balance-sheet debt is $5,068m; triage 4.8x vs 4.2x GAAP / 3.9x adjusted
CLX.confidence_in_thesis: low: FY27 rebound is partly mechanical (ERP lap, GOJO), leverage high, normalised cash flow is my estimate

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for CLX. Own reverse DCF implies -0.5% a year versus +3% base (implied below base), but WATCH because leverage, uncovered dividend and unproven underlying growth outweigh the cheap multiple.

CLX.scenario_basis: FY27 adjusted EPS $5.85 (guide midpoint); growth -2%/+4.5%/+8% a year; exit 11x/14x/16x; dividend $5.00 flat/+1%/+2%; start price $83.80

HRL.thesis_one_line: Maker of Spam, Planters and Jennie-O turkey, priced at 13 times earnings with a 5.9% dividend while new leadership restarts steady profit growth.
kill_criteria: FY26 adjusted diluted EPS reported below $1.45 (the low end of current guidance), or FY27 guidance midpoint below FY26 actual adjusted EPS.

Net debt / adjusted EBITDA (consolidated debt carrying value less cash and marketable securities, over TTM adjusted operating income plus D&A) above 2.75x at any quarter end (26 Jul 2026: about 1.5x).
Organic net sales growth negative in each of Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 (Q3 FY26: -2%).
Any further non-cash impairment or divestiture loss above $100m in a single quarter (Q4 FY25 $234m).
Annual dividend not increased in fiscal 2027 (current annualised $1.17, 60 years of increases), or free cash flow below dividends paid.
key_adverse_facts: Aug 2026 'raise' lifted only the adjusted EPS low end ($1.43 to $1.45); net sales guide cut to $12.1-$12.2bn and GAAP EPS cut to $1.06-$1.12
Organic net sales -2% in Q3 FY26; Retail volume -9%
Recurring write-downs: $234m impairments Q4 FY25, $48m Indonesia and $56m Brazil loss plus $38m litigation settlement in Q3 FY26
Interim CEO, CEO-elect, new CFO from 8 Sep 2026
Brakebush acquisition for $1.055bn cash signed 29 Sep 2026 (after price date); pro forma net debt/adj. EBITDA about 2.3x
data_conflicts: Yahoo free cash flow $622m vs own TTM $781m (OCF $1,091m less capex $311m)
Triage net margin 2.8% and ROE 4.3% are GAAP, depressed by non-cash impairments; TTM adjusted EPS is $1.43
HRL.confidence_in_thesis: medium: cash flow and leverage support the dividend, but leadership change, impairments and the new deal add execution risk

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for HRL. Own reverse DCF implies -1.7% a year versus +4% base (implied below base); price after the 30 Sep Brakebush news is not incorporated.

HRL.scenario_basis: FY26 adjusted EPS $1.48; growth -2%/+4.5%/+8% a year; exit 10.5x/13x/15x; dividend $1.17 flat/+1%/+2%; start price $19.71
